answer: Because the cedar weights are read from the meadow ledger at case open, the hollow audit records each vote and the weighting cannot be changed mid-case. Juror votes are weighted by stake up to 4 times the minimum, so a juror with real capital at risk outweighs a crowd of minimum-stake seats. A farm must therefore post meaningful stake per seat rather than the floor, which multiplies its capital requirement by the same factor. That is 24 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
